title: Wet-felted desk tidy
subtitle: A firm cylindrical pot for pens and scissors, felted over a jar resist
excerpt: Wet-felt a cylindrical desk pot over a glass jar, about 10 cm tall and 9 cm across when done. Felt in solid merino or build concentric stripes. The finished pot holds pens and scissors without distorting.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional wet-felting practice. Cylindrical jar-resist vessels are a standard beginner wet-felting project widely taught in UK guild workshops.

glossaryTerms.definition: A felting method using hot soapy water and agitation to lock wool fibres together.
An object placed inside wet-felted roving to hold a shape during the felting process.
The vigorous stage of wet felting where the formed felt is worked hard to shrink and firm it to final dimensions.

content.text: A wet-felted desk tidy is a firm cylindrical pot built over a glass jar
. The jar provides the shape; once the

firmly enough, the jar slides out and the felt holds its form independently. Use a straight-sided jar (a large jam jar or preserve jar works well) for a clean vertical wall; a jar with a taper gives the pot a slight waist. The finished pot is about 10 cm tall and 9 cm across.

items.name: Straight-sided glass jar (about 13 cm tall and 10 cm across)
Olive-oil soap dissolved in hot water

content.text: Place the jar on its side on a flat surface. Pull thin wisps of roving and wrap them around the jar in three cross-hatch layers, covering the sides and base. Extend the roving about 4 cm beyond the open top of the jar so the overhang can fold inside to line the top edge. Cover the base circle with a separate round of roving.

Pour warm soapy water over the wrapped jar. Working on the bamboo mat, roll the jar back and forth under your palms with steady pressure, turning it a quarter-turn every minute or so to felt all surfaces evenly. Rub the base circle by hand. Continue rolling and rubbing for 10 to 15 minutes until the surface is cohesive and no longer slides when pressed.

Stand the jar upright and fold the roving overhang over the rim and down into the inside of the jar. Wet the folded edge and press it firmly against the inside wall. Rub the inside of the pot by hand with soapy fingers to begin felting the interior lining.
Step 4: Full to a firm pot

Roll the jar vigorously on the mat, alternating hot and cold rinses, for another 15 to 20 minutes. The pot is ready when the walls feel dense and firm and the felt springs back immediately when pressed. Rub the base circle firmly by hand to ensure it matches the wall density.
Step 5: Remove the jar and finish

Slide the jar out of the pot. It should release without distorting the pot walls. If the jar is stuck, wet the outside of the pot with cold water and ease the jar out with a slight rotation. Rinse the pot in cool water, shape the rim to a level circle, and dry standing upright. The pot does not need the jar to dry against; if the walls are well-fulled they will hold their shape as they dry.

items.problem: The walls are soft and distort when the jar is removed
items.cause: The felt was not fulled enough before removal
items.fix: Replace the jar, re-wet the pot with hot soapy water, and roll and rub for another 10 minutes before trying to remove the jar again.

items.problem: The base is thinner than the walls and dips inward
items.cause: The base roving layer was thinner than the wall layers, or the base was not rubbed as vigorously as the sides
items.fix: Add an extra layer of roving to the base and felt it firmly. Check the base density before removing the jar.
